methodology_assessment.process_correction: Prior work often built correct restricted proofs before checking whether the exact statement was already known or whether the result crossed an asymptotic boundary. Future work should demand a primary-source theorem comparison before proof expansion, one theorem-sized first lemma, and an honest idle queue when no candidate passes all gates.

candidates.area: graph structure; distance profiles; metric dimension; kernelization
candidates.precise_problem: For each fixed t >= 1, is there C_t such that every finite simple undirected G with stw(G) <= t, every r >= 1, and every A subset V(G) of size k >= 1 has pc_r(G,k) <= C_t r^t k? First nontrivial target: t=3, O(r^3 k). pc_r counts distinct non-all-infinite vectors of distances to A truncated above r.
candidates.best_known_result: Beaudou et al. give O_t(r^(t+1)k) for treewidth t, asymptotically tight for general treewidth, and O(r^2 k) for outerplanar graphs. They state O_t(r^t k) for bounded simple treewidth as a conjecture; t=1,2 are covered.
candidates.remaining_gap: For stw >= 3, remove one factor r relative to general treewidth; asymptotic tightness is claimed conditional on the conjecture.

sources.source_type: primary preprint; v3 submission history 2025-12-13; manuscript body reports 2026-08-24, retained as a date-provenance discrepancy

sources.title: Joret and Rambaud, Neighborhood complexity of planar graphs
sources.specific_claim: Source of the general treewidth profile bounds and lower construction cited by Beaudou et al.

candidates.later_status: The latest accessible primary text still states the conjecture. Exact-title and citation-oriented follow-up checks found no matched resolution, but this is not exhaustive and simple-treewidth of the cited lower construction was not reconstructed.
candidates.first_lemma: Sufficient condition: an O(k)-size family of vertex guards, each of size at most 3, such that for each v with a finite r-profile to A one guard hits every v-a path of length <= r for every a in A. For fixed S, the truncated profile to A is determined by the truncated distance vector from v to S, giving at most (r+2)^3 possibilities per guard.
candidates.proof_attempt: Generic treewidth guard construction uses sets up to 2(t+1) vertices and yields r^(t+1). Outerplanar proof uses circular BFS-layer monotonicity. For simple treewidth 3, an LCA-closure component can have two marked attachments; both adhesion boundaries may matter. No proof collapses them to a 3-vertex guard or bounds their joint signatures by O(r^3). This fails as a proof route, not as a counterexample to the conjecture.
candidates.fast_falsifier: Search for simple-3-tree chains with two-sided LCA corridors and A on both sides that realize Omega(r^4 k); a finite example can refute only the guard-family lemma, not the asymptotic conjecture.
candidates.significance: Would improve a tight profile-complexity exponent for a broad structural graph class, with implications to metric dimension and distance-based kernelization.

conditional_mathematical_fact.statement: If for every G,A,r in the stw<=3 class there is a family of at most C|A| guards of size <=3, with each chosen guard intersecting every length<=r v-to-a path for all a in A, then pc_r(G,|A|) <= C|A|(r+2)^3.
conditional_mathematical_fact.status: elementary conditional counting implication; guard-family existence not proved; not a new graph theorem
conditional_mathematical_fact.proof_outline: For a fixed guard S, any shortest path of length at most r to a landmark intersects S, so its distance is min_{s in S}(dist(v,s)+dist(s,a)); a profile is determined by the truncated distance vector to S. There are at most (r+2)^3 such vectors. Sum over O(k) guards.
conditional_mathematical_fact.adversarial_caveat: A set guarding one landmark or one selected shortest path is insufficient. Two-sided decomposition corridors can require considering two adhesion boundaries; no correlation bound was proved.
